nodes.summary: Comparison theorem for one-dimensional BSDEs (Peng 1992; El Karoui–Peng–Quenez 1997). Under the hypotheses of `bsde_existsUnique` on two generators `g₁, g₂` and two terminal values `ξ₁, ξ₂`, if `ξ₁ ≥ ξ₂` almost surely and, for each `(t, y, z)`, `g₁(t, y, z) ≥ g₂(t, y, z)` almost surely, then the solutions satisfy `Y¹_t ≥ Y²_t` almost surely for every `t ∈ [0, T]`. S. Peng, Proc. ICM 2010, Vol. I, Theorem 1.2.
nodes.title: Comparison theorem for one-dimensional BSDEs

nodes.summary: Existence and uniqueness for BSDEs with Lipschitz generators (Pardoux–Peng 1990). Let `B` be a real Brownian motion with continuous paths and `F` its augmented filtration. nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness for BSDEs with Lipschitz generators

nodes.summary: Nonlinear Feynman–Kac formula, classical case (Peng 1991; Pardoux–Peng 1992). Let `b, σ, φ : ℝ → ℝ` be Lipschitz, `f(x, y, z)` Lipschitz on `ℝ³`, and let `X` solve the SDE `X_t = x + ∫_0^t σ(X_s) dB_s + ∫_0^t b(X_s) ds` (in the solution class of `MathlibExt.Probability.LipschitzSDEWanted.sde_lipschitz_existsUnique`). nodes.title: Nonlinear Feynman–Kac formula, classical case

nodes.summary: `F t` is generated by `B_s`, `s ≤ t`, together with the `P`-null measurable sets. This is the filtration of the BSDE theory (S. Peng, Proc. ICM 2010, Vol. I, §1.1, where the null sets are left implicit); the solution of a BSDE is adapted to it because of the Brownian martingale representation theorem.
nodes.title: Augmented Brownian filtration

nodes.summary: If the generator vanishes at `z = 0` along the constant `c` (`g(t, ω, c, 0) = 0`), then `(Y, Z) = (c, 0)` solves the BSDE with terminal value `c`. With uniqueness of solutions, this is the property `E^g[c] = c` of Peng's g-expectation, defined for generators with `g(·, y, 0) ≡ 0` (S. Peng, Proc. ICM 2010, Vol. I, §1.6, equation (1.19) and the sentence after it).
nodes.title: Constant solutions and constant preservation of g-expectations

nodes.summary: Solution of a one-dimensional BSDE on `[0, T]` (S. Peng, Proc. ICM 2010, Vol. I, §1.2, equation (1.7) and Theorem 1.1, with `m = d = 1`). can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
